exercises.why: **разбираешь** — разбира́ть (imperfective): to dismantle, to disassemble, to take apart, to deconstruct; to analyse, to parse; to agitate, to disturb, to trouble. Wiktionary: раз- + -бира́ть.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: All day I went over the events in my memory.
exercises.ru: Весь день я ___ в памяти произошедшие события.
exercises.why: **перебирал** — перебира́ть (imperfective): to sort out, to look through; (music) to finger (strings of a string musical instrument); to take in excess, to take too much; to recall, to turn over in one's mind. Wiktionary: пере- + -бира́ть.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: She arranges her bookshelves each month.
exercises.ru: Она ___ содержимое своих книжных полок каждый месяц.
exercises.why: **перебирает** — перебира́ть (imperfective): to sort out, to look through; (music) to finger (strings of a string musical instrument); to take in excess, to take too much; to recall, to turn over in one's mind. Wiktionary: пере- + -бира́ть.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: to take away, to seize, to collect; to capture, to take possession
to take something with hands, to take (mutually, together) (e.g. each other's hands)
to make one's way, to thread one's way, to pick one's way, to edge through
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: вы́бор — choice (option or decision); забра́ть — to take away, to seize, to collect; to capture, to take possession; бра́ться — to take something with hands, to take (mutually, together) (e.g. each other's hands); пробира́ться — to make one's way, to thread one's way, to pick one's way, to edge through.
